body: Some of the behaviors I tried to verify with tests but wasn't able to. Specifically, it seemed like `_find_enumeration_candidates` was never being triggered. They may well be bugs we should file separate issues for.

Tested locally, it works as expected with all symbol types (I've tested both enums and enum values too). Code looks good to me.

One issue I noticed is that the strikethrough is drawn too low and almost looks like an underline:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/37442b5e-55c5-4cac-b526-c6f5f56a7e4c)

See RichTextLabel's strikethrough drawing guide for a reference:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/7598b08ec2ccf6c5bbc2c2020f583fc625e3238b/scene/gui/rich_text_label.cpp#L1159-L1165

Additionally, you can get the font's underline width from the font metadata to use a line width (this is already done in RichTextLabel for both strikethrough and underline):

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/7598b08ec2ccf6c5bbc2c2020f583fc625e3238b/scene/gui/rich_text_label.cpp#L939-L943

Looks great now :slightly_smiling_face: 

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ec5608f2-16df-4b6e-bd17-335d8e4cd0c1)

And at 200% editor scale too:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ea60723d-dce1-4bcf-8243-2fa0a8cbbb64)

First of all I tested this a bit and it seems to work correctly :+1:  Skimming over the GDScript code, it seems fine on the small scale.

That being said, I don't like the approach this PR takes from an architectural standpoint.

This code adds too much coupling between GDScript and the editor. There exists a well defined API for how the GDScript module interacts with the editor in  `ScriptLanguage` other than that they should probably not know about each other, this includes things like `EditorHelp`.

Also the GDScript module has a well defined job: handling GDScript related things. Interacting with the documentation cache most certainly isn't GDScript related so this breaks cohesion IMO. I don't see why we have to iterate and join the documentation in GDScript specific code. There were no usages of `EditorHelp` in this file before, even the documentation tooltip feature managed to keep those concerns separated and only resolves documentation for locals in the GDScript module.

In my opinion we should attach symbol information to the completion options (the ones in the script language interface, not the ones in `CodeEdit`), the editor can use this symbol information to look for the correct documentation.

That's easier said than done, since there is no unified symbol model that would support locals at the moment. So please don't try to implement this! I'm just trying to say that the script language interface might need some refactoring to facilitate the addition of more IDE like features.

I know that Godot has this ["one problem one solution"](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/contributing/development/best_practices_for_engine_contributors.html#to-each-problem-its-own-solution) policy, and in this case I disagree with it, a lot of IDE like features share the need to work with certain symbols in one way or the other, encapsulating this in a flexible model and using it to implement such features seems like the best approach to me. That being said I acknowledge that this policy has brought Godot to were it is today, so if the team wants to move forward with this feature like it is implemented here, that's fine with me. The specific code in the functions looks mostly good and _should_ be fine to merge :)

I'll neither approve nor reject this, I'll just leave my opinion here, someone more familiar with the project should make this decision.

I haven't looked at the code, but from a usability perspective this looks good. I was not able to check all the possible usages of deprecation supported by this PR, but the few I did try worked well. I think the place where most users will come across this is deprecated engine functions, and those show up correctly as strikethrough in autocomplete now.
